question: round 6: does the drift family transfer across runtimes — rho of the bnb-NF4 delta against v3's W (family = quantization grid vs kernel ordering)
protocol: gemma-4-31B loaded in bnb NF4 on the same CUDA box, 5000 calib captions encoded (nf4_cap_states.pt); delta = pool mean minus each head's mu_txt; gain = ||delta @ Wt.T||; rand = random direction at matched norm; rho = gain / median head-space ||q||
findings: ANSWER: kernel ordering, not quantization grid. The NF4 delta is essentially orthogonal to the MLX delta (cos 0.083) — each runtime pair is its own drift family in direction
v3's suppression is family-specific: it nulls the trained MLX direction 2.5x below random (ratio 0.298 vs v1's 0.749) but shows ZERO suppression of the never-seen NF4 direction (0.925, random-level)
mitigating practical fact: the NF4 displacement is 3x smaller in norm (7.06 vs 21.52) — same-silicon quantization drifts far less than cross-silicon kernels, so the untransferred family matters less

BONUS: v5's compositional training largely overwrote v3's drift-nulling (MLX ratio 0.815 vs v3's 0.298) — the two augmentations compete for the same head capacity; the demo correctly serves v3, and a v6 would need to re-verify cross-runtime arms after compositional training
